title: Command E on a video never flattens the recording into a still
goal: Someone who knows Final Cut presses Command E on a video expecting Export. Today, with a title picked, it runs Merge Down, which bakes the title and the recording into one still picture: the timeline goes empty and the video is gone until they undo. Merging must never turn a clip into a still, and Command E on a video should do what the key rule says it does there.
notes: Reproduced by the manager pass 2026-10-15 20:40 with a scratch walk (/tmp/mgr-walk/cmd-e-on-a-video.json, steps: openSampleRecording, videoSeekMiddle, text tool, click 620,330, type 'Shipping today', Command Return, expectLayers 2 passes, expectPicked [Shipping today] passes, then {do: shortcut, key: e, modifiers: [command], menuItem: Merge Down}). Result: 'step 19 (expectLayers): 1 layer in the document, not at least 2; the first few: Tutorial Sample', and the after picture (queue/manager/shots/2026-10-15-cmd-e-on-a-video-after.png) shows the timeline with no clip and no tracks and the title baked into the picture. A plain {do: key} press said: 'command+e is Layer > Merge Down'. Code: Sources/Photonz/EditorCommands.swift ~1949-1951 (Command E = Merge Down on every document), EditorState+LayerOps.swift canMergeDown ~165-171 (only needs a picked layer that is not the bottom one), mergeLayers ~208-217 (bakes into a still). Export is Shift Command E (EditorCommands.swift ~422-437). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-entry-wt.html step 8 and video.html command menu print Export MP4 Command E; Final Cut's Command E is Share/Export; check Premiere's own Command E before choosing. Merge on two still layers on a picture must not change.
acceptance: On a video at Next defaults, open the sample recording, type a title over it, keep the title picked and press Command E: the recording is still a clip on the timeline with all its time, and nothing is baked into a still

Merge Down (menu row, right-click and key) is dimmed or refuses with a short canvas note whenever the layer or the one under it has time (a clip, or a layer with an in and an out), on any document, and still merges two still layers on a picture exactly as before

What Command E does on a video is settled by the key rule in UX-PATTERNS section 7 (Photoshop's key on a picture, Premiere's on a video) and the choice is named in the audit's rough list in one line citing section 7; the mock prints Command E for Export MP4
A walk at Next defaults proves the first item (types a title, presses the key, claims the clip and both layers are still there) and passes twice in a row
A core test pins that merging never takes a layer with time
Audit written under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced first with the manager's walk: after Command E the document had 1 layer (Tutorial Sample) and the title was baked in. Key rule (UX-PATTERNS §7): Premiere's Cmd E is Edit Original and its Export is Cmd M; Photoshop's Cmd E is Merge Down. So Cmd E stays Merge Down on every document and the mock's Export MP4 Cmd E loses the key; Export stays Shift Cmd E. Fix: PhotonzCore LayerMerge.swift (Layer.mayBeMerged / Layer.canMerge: no clip, sound, in/out or group holding one), used by canMergeDown, the new canMergeDown(id:) for the Layers row menu, and the mergeLayers guard. Test: MergeNeverTakesTimeTests. Walk: command-e-on-a-video-keeps-the-clip-walk, ok twice in a row; bucket-fills, menu-keys-do-what-they-say and row-menu-group still ok. Scripts/test.sh: 13291 tests passed.

Adversarial review: a Final Cut user pressing Cmd E on a clip now gets nothing at all (a dimmed row and no note). The task allowed dimmed-or-note, and Export is one modifier away in the File menu. A timeline clip bar's own right-click menu has no Merge Down; the Layers panel row is the only right-click home and it now dims through the same rule.

left rough, not filed: Cmd E on a clip is silent (no canvas note). Nobody is stopped by it and nothing is lost, so it does not clear the bar yet; file it if the user asks on the audit. Premiere's Cmd M for Export is not added because Cmd M is the Mac's Minimize.

Merge Down never takes a clip, sound, timed layer or group holding one (PhotonzCore LayerMerge.swift, MergeNeverTakesTimeTests), so Command E with a title over a recording leaves the clip and title on the timeline; pictures merge as before. Command E stays Merge Down on video per UX-PATTERNS §7 (Premiere: Cmd E Edit Original, Cmd M Export); Export stays Shift Cmd E.
